Radiology billing and coding

Radiology depends on information from others: the ordering provider, the facility and the scheduler. We catch mismatches between what was ordered, approved and read before they become denials.

Contact UsCall us

Billing challenges in radiology

Order and authorization mismatch

If a study is done with contrast but authorized without, or on a different body part, the claim may deny.

Professional and technical splits

Modifiers 26 and TC must reflect who did the read and who owns the equipment.

Diagnosis from the ordering provider

Coding depends on the indication provided and the final report, so missing history can leave a study hard to support.

Multi-state and multi-site reads

Teleradiology and multiple locations can multiply the enrollment and licensing to keep current.

Codes we commonly review

These are examples, not a full list. Coverage and coding rules vary by payer, so each claim is checked against the current rules and your documentation.

  • 70450–70470 CT head/brain
  • 71045–71048 chest X-ray
  • 72141–72158 spine MRI
  • 77065–77067 mammography
  • Modifiers 26, TC, LT and RT
